topic: Is a root canal actually painful?
title: root-canal-pain-truth
save_trigger: Someone who has been putting off a root canal wants the reassurance in writing, and wants to send it to whoever keeps telling them horror stories.

slides.kicker: We get asked this a lot
slides.headline: Is a root canal really as bad as everyone says?
slides.body: Short answer: the reputation comes from what the tooth felt like before treatment, not from the treatment itself.

slides.headline: The infection is the pain. The treatment is what stops it.
slides.body: People arrive already hurting, because an inflamed or infected pulp is one of the sharper things a tooth can do. The procedure removes that tissue. Most of what patients describe as root canal pain is the toothache that brought them in.

claims.text: Root canal treatment removes inflamed or infected pulp from inside the tooth.

slides.headline: You are numb before anything starts.
slides.body: The tooth and the area around it are anaesthetised first, and we check that you are numb before beginning. Most people describe the appointment as long rather than sharp. Individual experience varies, and we will stop and add more if you need it.

claims.text: Local anaesthetic is used during root canal treatment so the area is numb.
claims.source_title: American Association of Endodontists — Root Canal Treatment

slides.headline: Plan for about ninety minutes.
slides.body: It is not a quick appointment, and we would rather you hear that now than find out in the chair. Some teeth are done in one visit, others in two. Front teeth are usually faster than molars, which have more canals to clean.

slides.headline: Sore for a few days is normal. Worse is not.
slides.body: Expect tenderness when you bite for two or three days, the way a bruise is tender. That settles. Swelling that grows, or pain that climbs instead of fading, is a reason to call us rather than wait it out.

claims.text: Mild discomfort for a few days after root canal treatment is common and usually settles.
claims.source_title: American Association of Endodontists — Root Canal Treatment

slides.headline: The other option is losing the tooth.
slides.body: Extraction is a real choice and we will talk it through honestly. But replacing a tooth later is more work than keeping the one you have. If the tooth is restorable, keeping it is usually the less invasive path.

claims.text: Root canal treatment is used to save a tooth that would otherwise need removal.

slides.headline: Tell us before, not during.
slides.body: There are more options than most people realise, and they all work better when we know in advance. Raising a hand to pause is always allowed. Nobody here is going to be surprised that you are nervous about this one.

slides.headline: Send this to whoever keeps telling you the horror story.
slides.body: If you have been putting this off, booking the assessment is the part that actually ends the uncertainty. We will tell you what we see before we touch anything.

caption: Root canals have the worst reputation in dentistry and most of it is borrowed. Almost everyone who tells you the horror story is describing how the tooth felt in the days before they got treated, when the pulp was already inflamed and every heartbeat was landing in their jaw. That is the pain people remember. The appointment itself is done under local anaesthetic and the honest complaint we hear afterwards is that it was long, not that it was sharp. Plan for about ninety minutes, expect a few days of bite tenderness the way a bruise is tender, and call us if it climbs instead of fading. The part worth knowing: the alternative is usually losing the tooth, and replacing one later is more work than keeping the one you already have. What have you been told about root canals that you are not sure is true?
